definition: Elicit means to draw out or bring forth a response.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word elicit. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know elicit should be able to work it out from your sentence.

To invite a response is gentler than to elicit one — an invitation leaves the door open, while eliciting actively draws the response out.
Extract is stronger than elicit: what you elicit comes willingly once drawn, but what you extract is pulled out against resistance.

Evoke draws out feelings, memories, or images that come up on their own — an old photograph evokes a face, a certain slant of light evokes a winter. Elicit points at people and design: a response deliberately drawn out of someone, the answer or laugh a technique was built to produce.

A prompt is the small cue that triggers a response — a sticky note, a stage whisper, one leading question. Elicit is the fuller act of drawing the response out, often skillfully and by design; the prompt is only the nudge that starts it.
